Class.name: IAD.Skill.ObjectScriptRepair
Class.Description: Hard-gate checklist for the 10 most common ObjectScript mistakes

XData.name: SUMMARY
XData.Data: name: objectscript-repair description: Hard-gate checklist for the 10 most common ObjectScript mistakes. Checks code before this agent presents it. tags: - objectscript - repair - code-review

XData.name: INSTRUCTIONS
XData.Data:
# ObjectScript Repair — Hard Gate
Do not show ObjectScript code until this checklist passes.
## Review Checklist
For each item, check the generated code and flag any violations:
- [ ] **QUIT/RETURN**: No `Quit <value>` inside TRY/CATCH or loops - [ ] **Method calls**: Intra-class calls use `..MethodName()` syntax - [ ] **Error handling**: Uses `$$$ThrowOnError` / `$$$ISERR` macros, not raw status checks - [ ] **THROW**: Never throws a `%Status` directly — uses `%Exception` objects - [ ] **Precedence**: Complex arithmetic has explicit parentheses - [ ] **Transactions**: TRollback checks `$TLevel > 0` first - [ ] **NEW**: No `New` command inside method/procedure blocks - [ ] **%TimeStamp**: Uses `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` format, not ISO 8601 with `T` - [ ] **%Status returns**: Methods returning %Status use `$$$OK` and check with `$$$ISOK`/`$$$ISERR` - [ ] **Globals**: No temporary data stored in globals when locals suffice
## Output Format
If violations found:
> ⚠️ ObjectScript review flagged [N] issues — correcting before showing: > > - [rule]: [what was wrong] → [correct pattern]
Then show the corrected code.
If clean:
> ✅ ObjectScript review passed.
Then show the code.

Class.name: IAD.Skill.ObjectScriptGuardrails
Class.Description: All-in-one hard gate for ObjectScript code — 13-item safety checklist

XData.name: SUMMARY
XData.Data: name: objectscript-guardrails description: All-in-one hard gate for ObjectScript code. Works without MCP connected — the instructions alone provide a 13-item safety checklist. tags: - objectscript - guardrails - code-review - core

XData.name: INSTRUCTIONS
XData.Data:
# ObjectScript — Hard Gate
**Do not show ObjectScript code until this checklist passes.**
## HARD GATE Checklist
- [ ] **Quit/Return**: No `Quit value` inside For/While/Try — use `Return value` - [ ] **Postfix syntax**: `Quit:key=""` — NO spaces in condition, alone on its own line - [ ] **$IsObject**: Check `'$IsObject(obj)` after every `%OpenId` before touching properties - [ ] **SQL table name**: Last dot = schema separator. `Catalog.Item` → SQL `Catalog.Item` (not `Catalog_Item`) - [ ] **SQLCODE**: `0` = success (falsy). Check `SQLCODE = 0` not just `SQLCODE` - [ ] **HTML escaping**: `&` FIRST, then `<`, then `>` - [ ] **Arithmetic**: Left-to-right, no precedence. Use `1.8` not `9/5`. Parenthesize everything - [ ] **$ListBuild()**: Empty list is `""` not `$ListBuild()` — `$ListLength($ListBuild()) = 1` - [ ] **%Status**: Use `$$$ISERR(sc)` / `$$$ThrowOnError(sc)`. Never return `$$$OK` after catching an error - [ ] **Transactions**: `If $TLevel > 0 { TROLLBACK }` — never `Return` inside TSTART without rollback - [ ] **Storage blocks**: NEVER write `Storage Default { ... }` in UDL — omit entirely. IRIS auto-generates storage. Writing one causes ERROR #5559 in IRIS 2025.1+. - [ ] **%INLIST in ObjectScript**: `%INLIST` is SQL-only. In ObjectScript method code use `$ListFind(list, value) > 0`. Writing `Return (x %INLIST list)` causes ERROR #1010. - [ ] **`'=` in SQL strings**: `'=` is the ObjectScript not-equal operator. Inside SQL string literals, use `<>`. `"WHERE Tags '= ''"` → parser sees `'` as start of SQL string.
## Output Format
If violations found:
> ⚠️ ObjectScript review flagged [N] issues — correcting: > > - [rule]: [wrong] → [correct]
Then show corrected code.
If clean:
> ✅ ObjectScript review passed.
Then show code.
## Quick Reference
```objectscript // WRONG → CORRECT Quit 0 (inside For) → Return 0 Quit:key = "" → Quit:key="" ..%OpenId(id).Prop → Set obj=..%OpenId(id) If '$IsObject(obj){...} SELECT FROM Catalog_Item → SELECT FROM Catalog.Item If SQLCODE { "not found" } → If SQLCODE = 100 { "not found" } celsius * 9 / 5 + 32 → (celsius * 1.8) + 32 Set lst = $ListBuild() → Set lst = ""
// Storage / Operators: Storage Default { <Type>...</Type> } → (omit entirely — IRIS auto-generates) Return (tag %INLIST myList) → Return ($ListFind(myList, tag) > 0) "WHERE Tags '= ''" → "WHERE Tags <> ''" ```

Class.name: IAD.Skill.InteropDebugging
Class.Description: Manages and observes IRIS Interoperability productions — lifecycle, logs, queues, and message tracing

XData.name: SUMMARY
XData.Data: name: interop-debugging description: Manages and observes IRIS Interoperability productions — lifecycle, logs, queues, and message tracing. tags: - interoperability - ensemble - debugging - production

XData.name: INSTRUCTIONS
XData.Data:
# Interoperability Debugging
## Production Lifecycle
Use `iris_production` for all lifecycle operations.
**Check status first** — always establish baseline state before any action:
```objectscript // Via iris_execute when iris_production returns "Invalid Production" Set state = ##class(Ens.Director).GetProductionState(.sc) Set prodName = ##class(Ens.Director).GetActiveProductionName() ```
State values: `$$$EnsProductionRunning`, `$$$EnsProductionStopped`, `$$$EnsProductionTroubled`, `$$$EnsProductionSuspended`.
**Hot-apply config changes** — use `UpdateProduction()`, not stop+start:
```objectscript // Correct — zero downtime, no message loss Set sc = ##class(Ens.Director).UpdateProduction()
// Wrong — drops in-flight messages Set sc = ##class(Ens.Director).StopProduction(30, 0) Set sc = ##class(Ens.Director).StartProduction("MyApp.Production") ```
## MCP Tool Flow
### Investigating a production problem
1. **`iris_production`** — check status with `full_status=true`. See which components are running, faulted, or disabled. 2. **`iris_interop_query`** — check queue depths if you suspect backlog. High depth on a specific component indicates a bottleneck or fault there. 3. **`iris_interop_query`** — search messages by body content, session ID, sender, or time range to trace a failed transaction end-to-end. 4. **`iris_get_log`** — fetch component-level log entries filtered to the component and time window of interest. Look for `ERROR` or `WARNING` severity. 5. **`iris_message_body(message_id)`** — read a specific message body by ID. PHI-gated: pass `acknowledgePhi=true` if the body contains protected health information.
### Recovering a faulted production
If the production is stuck or partially started, use the Management Portal "Recover" action, or via ObjectScript:
```objectscript // Force-recover a stuck production — only when graceful stop fails Set sc = ##class(Ens.Director).StopProduction(10, 1) ```
Never force-stop (`force=1`) unless a graceful stop has already timed out. Force-stop drops in-flight messages.
## Log Investigation
**`iris_get_log`** — primary tool for Interoperability log entries. Filter by component name and severity.
**`journal_search`** — search the IRIS journal for global-level changes. Use when a message body was modified but the Interop log shows no errors — the journal captures writes at the storage level.
## Key Rules
- **Namespace matters** — every tool accepts a `namespace` parameter. Productions in `HSCUSTOM` or application-specific namespaces require the correct namespace explicitly set. - **Do not restart to fix a config change** — use `UpdateProduction()`. Restart loses in-flight messages. - **`EnableConfigItem` not `StartConfigItem`** — `StartConfigItem` / `StopConfigItem` do not exist. Use `EnableConfigItem(name, 1/0, 1)`. - **OnRequest signature** — override must declare request as `%Library.Persistent`, not a typed subclass. IRIS validates signature against the base class at compile time.
## Output Format
When reporting production state:
> **Production**: `MyApp.Productions.Main` — RUNNING > **Components**: 12 running, 0 faulted, 2 disabled > **Queue depth**: BusinessProcess.OrderHandler: 0, BusinessOperation.SendHL7: 3
When tracing a message failure:
> **Session** `12345`: Failed at `BusinessOperation.SendHL7` — ERROR: Connection refused > **Fix**: Check the outbound adapter host/port configuration for SendHL7

Class.name: IAD.Skill.IrisNavigation
Class.Description: Deep codebase discovery and namespace exploration using read-only IRIS tools

XData.name: SUMMARY
XData.Data: name: iris-navigation description: Deep codebase discovery and namespace exploration using read-only IRIS tools. Bridges raw MCP tool data to architectural understanding. tags: - objectscript - navigation - codebase - read-only

XData.name: INSTRUCTIONS
XData.Data:
# ObjectScript Semantic Navigation
This skill provides strategies for mapping out ObjectScript codebases using the available MCP tools.
## Discovery Strategy
### 1. Symbol Anchoring
Before editing, always locate the **Symbol Anchor** (the definition of the class or method you intend to change).
- **Tool**: `iris_symbols(query)` — searches the live IRIS namespace by name pattern (supports `*` wildcards) - **Tool**: `iris_symbols_local(workspace_path)` — parses `.cls` files on disk via tree-sitter when IRIS is unavailable - **Tool**: `iris_search` — full-text regex search across all IRIS documents in a namespace; use when symbol lookup is too narrow and you need to find arbitrary patterns in source - **Strategy**: Don't just search for the name; check the `containerName` to confirm you are in the correct package.
### 2. Dependency Tracing
When changing a signature, use **Upstream Tracing** to find every caller.
- **Tool**: `docs_introspect(class_name)` — fetches the full class definition from `%Dictionary`, including all methods, parameters, return types, and inheritance chain - **Tool**: `iris_symbols(query="ClassName.*")` — list all members of a class - **Tool**: `iris_execute_method` — invoke a ClassMethod directly without ObjectScript boilerplate; useful for spot-checking return values during tracing - **Tool**: `iris_doc_search` — searches docs.intersystems.com via Algolia when you need reference material on a system class or API - **Strategy**: Read each caller's containing file before modifying. If a method is called from multiple packages, plan all edits before touching any file.
### 3. Hierarchical Exploration
ObjectScript heavily uses inheritance (`Extends`).
- **Strategy**: If a method is missing in the current file, check the `Extends` list. - **Tool**: `docs_introspect(class_name)` — reveals the full inherited interface including superclass chain. - **Tool**: `find_subclass_implementations` — find all subclass overrides of a method in the full inheritance hierarchy; essential when changing a base class method that subclasses may override differently - **Strategy**: Run `iris_symbols("SuperClass.*")` to list members inherited from a superclass.
### 4. Dynamic Dispatch Resolution
When code uses `$classmethod(var, method)` or `$method(obj, method)` patterns, the target class is not known statically.
- **Tool**: `resolve_dynamic_dispatch` — find all classes that implement a given method; use this to enumerate every possible dispatch target before concluding what a call site does.
### 5. Interoperability Routing
For Ensemble/Interoperability codebases, message routing is defined in MessageMap tables, not plain method calls.
- **Tool**: `extract_message_map_routing` — extract Ensemble MessageMap routing tables from a production or business process; use this before tracing message flow through an interop codebase.
## Bridging the Gap
When this agent receives a list of symbols from `iris_symbols`, it should follow this reasoning:
1. "I see `Package.Class:Method` at line 10." 2. "I will now call `docs_introspect('Package.Class')` to confirm the method signature and see what it overrides." 3. "I will search for `Package.Class` with `iris_symbols` and look for classes that `Extend` it."
## Guidelines
- Never assume a symbol is unique until verified by `iris_symbols`. - Always call `docs_introspect` on any class you did not write before editing it — the live definition may differ from what you can infer from filenames alone. - Use `iris_search` when you need to find a pattern across all documents in the namespace (not just classes — includes routines, includes, and CSP files).
## Related skills
- **objectscript-repair** — when navigation reveals a multi-class failure that needs coordinated fixes - **interop-debugging** — if the codebase you're navigating is an Interoperability production
